## Secrets

The chart never writes production secrets: it expects them in the namespace, created by hand or
brought from your vault by the External Secrets Operator (on by default, from the
`ClusterSecretStore` named by `global.externalSecrets.storeRef`).

**What you will be able to do:** create every secret the instance needs, and rotate them.

### What the instance reads

| Secret | Keys | Read by |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `choregos-api-secrets` (`global.apiSecretRef`) | `session-secret`, `run-token-private-key`; optional `run-token-public-key`, `session-secret-previous`, `secrets-keks` | API; the run-token key and `secrets-keks` by the orchestrator too |
| the same, for GitHub | `github-app-id`, `github-app-private-key`, `github-webhook-secret`; optional `github-app-client-id`, `github-app-client-secret` | API and orchestrator |
| `global.oidc.secretRef` | `client-secret` | API |
| `global.database.secretRef` | `url` | API, orchestrator |
| `global.gateway.secretRef` | `master-key` | orchestrator |
| `global.objectStore.secretRef` | `access-key`, `secret-key` | API |
| `global.memory.tokenSecret` | `token` | orchestrator |

### Generate them

```shell
openssl rand -base64 48
openssl ecparam -name prime256v1 -genkey -noout
python3 -c "import os,base64;print('k1:'+base64.b64encode(os.urandom(32)).decode())"
```

- **`session-secret`** (the first command) signs the session cookie and the sign-in handshakes. It is
  required; on a deployed instance it must be at least 32 bytes.
- **`run-token-private-key`** (the second) signs the tokens of agent runs: the orchestrator mints
  them, the API checks them, so **both** must read the same key.
- **`secrets-keks`** (the third) seals the connector secrets people type in the console. Without it,
  typing a secret answers `409`.

```shell
kubectl -n choregos create secret generic choregos-api-secrets \
  --from-literal=session-secret="$SESSION_SECRET" \
  --from-file=run-token-private-key=run-token.pem \
  --from-literal=secrets-keks="$KEKS"
```

With External Secrets, put the same properties under `choregos/api` in your vault; add
`global.secrets.keksInExternalSecret: true` once `secrets-keks` exists there.

### The key that seals connector secrets

`secrets-keks` is a list `id:base64`, the first entry sealing and the others only opening. **Losing it
loses every sealed value**, and a database backup alone reveals none of them. Keep it in your vault,
backed up.

To rotate it: put the new key first (`k2:…,k1:…`), redeploy, run `choregos admin secrets rewrap` as
the platform administrator, and remove the old key only once no database backup older than the rewrap
can still be restored.

### Rotating the others

- **Session secret:** move the old value to `session-secret-previous`, put the new one in
  `session-secret`, redeploy, and remove the previous one after 8 hours.
- **Run-token key:** the API and the orchestrator read the same Secret, so both take the new key at
  their restart. A run started before can no longer post its result: rotate it in a quiet window, when
  no run is in flight.

The step-by-step:
[secret rotation runbook](https://github.com/VargaFoundation/choregos/blob/v0.26.0/docs/runbooks/secret-rotation.md).
`global.devSecrets: true` generates everything for a bench; it is refused in `staging` and `prod`.

---

## Security model

Choregos assumes **an agent may attempt anything**, by mistake or by injection, and that a member of
one organisation will try to read another's. This page is the digest; the full model, with what is
not guarded, is the
[security reference](https://github.com/VargaFoundation/choregos/blob/v0.26.0/docs/security.md).

### Organisations are isolated in the database

Every request declares the organisations it may see, and PostgreSQL's row-level security refuses the
rest; a request that declares nothing sees nothing. That is why the API must connect as a role that
is **not** a superuser (a superuser ignores row-level security): in `staging` and `prod` it refuses to
start otherwise.

### Agents run in a sandbox

- One pod per run: non-root, no capabilities, a seccomp profile, no service-account token, required
  by the Kyverno policies in `infra/policies`. Set `global.runner.runtimeClass` to run every agent pod
  under gVisor or Kata; a project's policy can demand gVisor.
- A run holds only its own short-lived token. It never holds a provider key (the model gateway gets
  the run's own capped key), nor a connector's credential (the API calls tools for it).
- Writes outside the work item's allowed paths, and to the denied paths of the project's policy, are
  refused; the result is checked by the workflow's gates, not trusted.

### Network: three layers

1. The organisation's network list, which an administrator manages (**Admin › Network**), under a
   ceiling the operator sets (`global.egress.ceiling`).
2. A per-run egress proxy (`global.egress.enabled: true`), the wall for host, port and connection rate.
3. Your cluster's network policies.

The proxy cannot see inside TLS: methods, paths and headers are invisible to it. Allow hosts, not
URLs.

### Tokens and their scopes

| Scope | Opens | Never opens |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `*` | the REST API and the CLI | the MCP and A2A doors |
| `mcp:read`, `mcp:write` | the MCP door, optionally one project | the REST API |
| `a2a` | the A2A door, optionally one project | the REST API |
| an application's token | the A2A door, on its project, 365 days at most | everything else |

Tokens are stored as digests and shown once. **A decision** (approving a specification, a merge, a
release) is taken by a person signed in to the console, never by a token, an MCP client or an A2A
caller, and the sensitive ones ask that person to sign in again.

### Secrets

Connector secrets typed in the console are sealed with AES-256-GCM under a key the deployment holds
(`secrets-keks`): a database dump reveals nothing, and losing the key loses the values
([Secrets](secrets.md)).

### Audit

Every sign-in, token, door call, decision and change of rights is in the audit log (**Admin ›
Audit**), under the same organisation isolation as the rest.

### Supply chain

The images are signed with cosign (keyless), with an SBOM and SLSA provenance attached; the Kyverno
policies can require digest references. Hosted agents' images can be required to carry a trusted
signature (`global.images.hostedCosign: enforce`).

### Reporting a vulnerability

Follow [SECURITY.md](https://github.com/VargaFoundation/choregos/blob/v0.26.0/SECURITY.md); do not
open a public issue.

---

## Upgrades

**What you will be able to do:** move an instance to a new version without losing work in flight.

### Before you upgrade

1. **Read the release notes** of every version between yours and the target, on the
   [GitHub releases](https://github.com/VargaFoundation/choregos/releases), and the "Upgrading to …"
   sections of the
   [deployment reference](https://github.com/VargaFoundation/choregos/blob/v0.26.0/docs/deployment.md#upgrading-to-024).
   A breaking change says what to rename or set before you upgrade.
2. **Back up** the platform database and Temporal's, to the same instant ([Backups](backups.md)).
   The migrations change the schema; restoring a backup is the only way back.
3. Upgrade one minor version at a time when the notes say so.

### Upgrade

The same command as the install, with the new version:

```shell
helm upgrade --install choregos oci://ghcr.io/vargafoundation/charts/choregos \
  --version 0.26.0 --namespace choregos -f my-values.yaml
```

- The database migrations run as a Helm hook **before** the new API starts
  (`python -m choregos_api.migrate`, in a Job that waits for the database up to 300 seconds). With an
  embedded database the hook runs after the install instead: keep `choregos-api.migrations.hook` as
  the chart sets it.
- Work items in flight finish on the workflow version they started on; Temporal keeps their position
  across the restart of the workers.
- The images follow the chart's version.

### Check it

```shell
kubectl -n choregos get pods
kubectl -n choregos get jobs -l app.kubernetes.io/instance=choregos
curl -s https://choregos.example.com/api/v1/edition
```

**What you should see:** every pod `Running` on the new images, the job `choregos-migrations-<revision>`
completed, and the edition answer's `version` naming the new version.

### When it goes wrong

| Symptom | What to do |
| --- | --- |
| the migration Job fails | read its logs; the API did not start on the new version, the old pods still serve. Fix the cause, then run the upgrade again |
| the API refuses to start after the upgrade | its log names the setting; most often a value the release notes asked to change |
| you must go back | `helm rollback` restores the previous pods, not the previous schema: restore the database backup taken before the upgrade, then roll back |

Upgrading Temporal itself has its own
[runbook](https://github.com/VargaFoundation/choregos/blob/v0.26.0/docs/runbooks/temporal-upgrade.md).

### Upgrading to 0.26

0.26 brings [assistants](../use/assistants.md): a plugin may ship one, an organisation installs it for
an audience, and people converse with it in the console, from an MCP client or in an embedded frame.
Nothing changes for an organisation that installs none. The migrations run with the chart's job as
usual. The full table is in the
[deployment reference](https://github.com/VargaFoundation/choregos/blob/v0.26.0/docs/deployment.md#upgrading-to-026); what you do is:

1. **Bound the token exchange.** Set `CHOREGOS_TOKEN_EXCHANGE_AUDIENCES` to a JSON list of your sources'
   audiences (in `global.extraEnv`) before binding a need that uses the person's identity
   (`user_exchange`). Unset, a connector's editor chooses any audience the identity provider allows. See
   the [review of the person's identity](https://github.com/VargaFoundation/choregos/blob/v0.26.0/docs/security.md).
2. **Prepare the identity provider.** `user_exchange` needs token exchange (RFC 8693) enabled for the
   API's client and limited to those audiences. A standing delegation needs `offline_access` with
   bounded, revocable offline sessions. See [Identity](identity.md).
3. **Give conversation suites a model.** An assistant's conversation suites gate the promotion of its
   agent version, and a judge model scores their rubrics (`conversation_judge_model`, else the `strong`
   model profile). With no gateway key, a version whose assistant ships suites is refused promotion
   with the reason. `conversation_suites_require_model=false` opts out, and no check then runs.
4. **Pick a quiet hour.** The migration that makes `/responses` sessions durable closes the ones open at
   upgrade time. Matters only if you use hosted prompt agents.
5. **List the host origins** of an embedded assistant in the installation's `config.embed_origins`; nothing
   else to deploy. Accounts connected before 0.26 are connected again once.

:::caution Delegated tasks
The standing delegation ships, but its decision record
([ADR 0137](https://github.com/VargaFoundation/choregos/blob/v0.26.0/docs/adr/0137-a-standing-read-only-delegation.md)) stays proposed until the works council has
given its opinion and the data protection impact assessment is done. Do not offer delegated tasks to
people before then.
:::

---

## API overview

Everything the console does goes through the REST API, under `/api/v1` on your instance. The
[REST API guide](../integrate/rest.md) walks through a first script; this page is the map.

### The OpenAPI document

The API is described by an OpenAPI 3 document, the contract the console and the CLI are generated
against:
[`packages/contracts/openapi.yaml`](https://github.com/VargaFoundation/choregos/blob/v0.26.0/packages/contracts/openapi.yaml).
Take the version of your instance (`GET /api/v1/edition` says which). The MCP and A2A doors are not
in it: they speak their own protocols ([MCP](../integrate/mcp.md), [A2A](../integrate/a2a.md)).

### Conventions

| | |
| --- | --- |
| Base path | `/api/v1` |
| Authentication | `Authorization: Bearer chg_…`, a token of scope `*` ([REST guide](../integrate/rest.md#1-get-a-full-access-token)); the console uses a session cookie |
| A project in a path | its UUID, `org:slug`, `org/slug`, or a bare slug when it is unique |
| A work item in a path | its UUID or its key (`BIL-12`) |
| Lists | `?cursor=…&limit=…` (1 to 200, 50 by default); the answer is `{"items": [...], "meta": {"next_cursor", "has_more"}}` |
| Errors | RFC 9457 problems ([Error codes](errors.md#the-rest-api)) |
| Concurrent changes | send the version you read (`base_version`, `base_revision`); a `409 stale_base` says someone changed it first |
| Request ids | every answer carries `X-Request-Id` |
| Unknown keys | refused (`422`): a typo does not pass silently |

### Resources

| Area | Main paths |
| --- | --- |
| You and your tokens | `GET /me`, `GET POST /me/tokens`, `DELETE /me/tokens/{id}` |
| Organisations | `GET POST /orgs`, `PATCH /orgs/{org}` |
| Projects | `GET POST /orgs/{org}/projects`, `GET PATCH /projects/{id}`, `GET /projects/{id}/readiness` |
| Applications | `GET POST /projects/{id}/machine-accounts`, `POST /projects/{id}/machine-accounts/{slug}/tokens` |
| Workflows | `GET /projects/{id}/workflows`, `GET PUT /projects/{id}/workflows/{name}`, `POST /projects/{id}/workflows/validate`, `GET PUT /projects/{id}/workflow-routing` |
| Work items | `GET POST /projects/{id}/work-items`, `GET /work-items/{id}`, its `/timeline`, `/artifacts`, `/runs` |
| Decisions | `POST /work-items/{id}/decisions` (a person's session only) |
| Triggers | `GET /projects/{id}/triggers`, `POST /projects/{id}/triggers/{name}/token`, `POST /webhooks/triggers/{org}/{project}/{name}` |
| Runs | `GET /runs/{id}`, `/runs/{id}/events`, `/transcript`, `/logs`, `/diff` |
| Agents | `GET POST /orgs/{org}/agents`, `POST /orgs/{org}/agents/{slug}/versions/publish`, `PUT /projects/{id}/agents/{slug}` (pin) |
| Skills | `GET POST /orgs/{org}/skills`, `POST /orgs/{org}/skills/import`, `POST /orgs/{org}/skills/{slug}/versions` |
| Connectors and tools | `GET POST /orgs/{org}/connectors`, `POST /orgs/{org}/connectors/{name}/discover`, `PATCH /orgs/{org}/connectors/{name}/operations/{operation}` |
| Network | `GET /orgs/{org}/egress`, `POST /orgs/{org}/egress/rules`, `POST /orgs/{org}/egress/requests` |
| Plugins | `GET /orgs/{org}/plugins`, `POST /orgs/{org}/plugins/install` |
| Policy | `GET PUT /projects/{id}/policy`, `PUT /orgs/{org}/policy-ceiling` |
| The instance | `GET /edition` (public: edition and version) |

Paths are relative to `/api/v1`.

### Rate limits

Authenticated REST calls are not rate-limited by the API. Sign-in and webhook routes are limited per
client address (600 a minute by default, `429` with `Retry-After`). The MCP and A2A doors have their
own limits (120 calls a minute per token).

---

## Error codes

What each door answers when it refuses, and what to do about it. The A2A codes below are checked
against the door's code in the repository's tests: a code the door gains or loses without this page
turns the build red.

### The A2A door

**HTTP answers**, before the JSON-RPC call is read. The body is `{"error": "<message>"}`; a `401` or
`403` also carries a `WWW-Authenticate: Bearer` header.

| HTTP | Means | What to do |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `401` | no token, or an unknown, revoked, expired token, or an application that was removed | send a live token with the `a2a` scope |
| `403`, `insufficient_scope` | a token without the `a2a` scope (a full-access token included) | create an `a2a` token, or an application's token |
| `403`, bound to a project | the token is bound to another project | use that project's token |
| `403`, origin refused | a web page called the door | call it from a server, not a browser |
| `404` | no such organisation, or none the token can see | check the organisation in the URL |
| `413` | the message is larger than the door or the project takes | send smaller files |
| `429` | more than 120 calls a minute on this token | wait for `Retry-After` |

**JSON-RPC errors**, in an HTTP `200` (a `400` for `-32700` and `-32600`). In A2A 1.0, `error.data` is a
list whose first element is a `google.rpc.ErrorInfo`; refused fields come in a `google.rpc.BadRequest`.

| Code | Name | When | What to do |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `-32700` | parse error | the body is not JSON | send JSON |
| `-32600` | invalid request | not a JSON-RPC 2.0 object, a batch, no `method` | send one JSON-RPC object |
| `-32601` | method not found | a method neither 0.3.0 nor 1.0 has, or an `A2A-Version` header that disagrees with the method | use one version's names |
| `-32602` | invalid params | no or unknown skill, a missing `message`, a bad `messageId`, too many parts, a file not in base64 or too large, a file by `uri`, fields the workflow refuses (`error.data.errors`), no right to open work items | read the message; it names the field |
| `-32603` | internal error | a file could not be stored; nothing was created | send again |
| `-32001` | task not found | an unknown task id, or one this token cannot see; a stream whose token stopped working | check the id and the token |
| `-32002` | task not cancelable | the task is over, its workflow is not running, or you may not stop work items | nothing to cancel |
| `-32003` | push notifications not supported | push needs a `chg_` token, and the instance's secrets key | use a token, ask your operator |
| `-32004` | unsupported operation | `ListTasks`, or a reply to a task: a decision is taken in the console, at `decision_url` | keep task ids; decide in the console |
| `-32005` | content type not supported | the skill does not take this media type | add it to the workflow's `a2a.input_modes` |
| `-32007` | extended card not configured | `GetExtendedAgentCard`: the card is already read with a token | read the card |
| `-32009` | version not supported | an `A2A-Version` other than `0.3` and `1.0` | send `0.3`, `1.0`, or no header |
| `-32050` | budget exhausted | the daily write budget: 50 for a person, with the MCP door; an application's own (500 by default) | wait, or raise the application's budget |
| `-32051` | too many streams | a sixth stream open on one token | close one |

### The MCP door

| Answer | Means | What to do |
| --- | --- | --- |
| HTTP `400`, unsupported protocol version | the client speaks a version other than `2025-11-25`, `2025-06-18`, `2025-03-26` | update the client |
| HTTP `401` | no token, or an unknown, revoked, expired one; with OAuth, a token of the wrong audience or issuer | mint a token, or sign in again |
| HTTP `403`, `insufficient_scope` | a full-access token, or OAuth without an MCP scope | mint an `mcp:read` or `mcp:write` token |
| HTTP `403`, *sign in to the console once* | OAuth: the identity provider knows the person, Choregos does not yet | sign in to the console |
| HTTP `403`, bound to a project | the token belongs to another project | use the project's door or token |
| HTTP `404` | the project in `/mcp/projects/…` does not exist | check `org:slug` |
| HTTP `405` | a `GET` or `DELETE`: the door has no stream and no session | nothing: the protocol allows it |
| HTTP `413` | a message over 1 MiB | send less |
| HTTP `429` | more than 120 calls a minute on this token | wait for `Retry-After` |
| `-32601` | an unknown method | |
| `-32602`, *Unknown tool* | a tool that does not exist, or that your token or role may not use | use a token with `mcp:write`, or ask for the right |
| a tool result with `isError`, `budget_exhausted` | 50 writes a day through the MCP and A2A doors | wait |
| a tool result with `isError`, other text | a missing `project`, an unknown work item, no right to open one, invalid arguments | read the message |
| `[result_truncated: …]` at the end of a result | the result was longer than 60,000 characters | narrow the search |

### HTTP triggers

| HTTP | Means |
| --- | --- |
| `202` | accepted: `outcome` is `created_work_item`, `already_open`, `reopened` or `ignored`; `duplicate: true` for a delivery received before |
| `401` | an invalid trigger token, or a missing or wrong `X-Choregos-Signature` |
| `404` | no such organisation, project or trigger, or a trigger without a token yet |
| `409` | the project's tracker is external |
| `413` | a body over 256 KiB |
| `422` | not a JSON object, no text or number at the `key` pointer, or fields the workflow refuses |
| `429` | too many calls from one address (600 a minute by default) |

See [HTTP triggers](../integrate/triggers.md).

### The REST API

Errors are RFC 9457 problems (`application/problem+json`): `type`, `title`, `status`, and often
`detail`, `errors` (each with `loc`, `msg` and sometimes `code`, `line`, `column`) and `code`.

| Status | Means |
| --- | --- |
| `400` | the request breaks a rule of the platform; `title` names it |
| `401` | `unknown or revoked API token`, `expired API token`, or no session |
| `403` | the token is for the MCP or A2A door (the REST API needs the `*` scope), the role lacks the right, or a change with the session cookie from another origin |
| `404` | not found, or not visible to you; an ambiguous bare project slug asks for `org/slug` |
| `409` | a conflict; `code` says which ([below](#conflict-codes)) |
| `422` | the body does not match the contract (`Invalid request`), or a document the platform refuses (`errors` lists each problem) |
| `429` | too many sign-in or webhook calls from one address |
| `500` | an internal error: give the `correlation_id` and the `X-Request-Id` to your operator |
| `502` | an external system (a tracker, a model gateway, an MCP server) failed; `retry_after` when it may pass |

#### Conflict codes

| `code` | Means | What to do |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `stale_base` | someone published another version since the one you read (`latest_version` or `latest_revision` says which) | read it, apply your change again |
| `no_change` | the new version is the same as the current one | nothing |
| `eval_failed` | the agent's evals failed on the new version | fix the version, or the eval |
| `egress_required` | a host the change needs is not in the organisation's network list | an administrator allows it, or passes `allow_egress: true` |
| `gateway_required` | the organisation requires its MCP gateway; a direct MCP server is refused | add the server through the gateway |
| `gateway_not_configured` | the server is to go through a gateway that is not set up | set up the gateway |
| `gateway_in_use` | removing a gateway that connectors still use | move them first |

#### Workflow validation

When a workflow is refused, `errors` lists each problem with its `code`, `line` and `column`:

| Code | Means |
| --- | --- |
| `yaml.syntax`, `yaml.not_a_mapping` | the file is not a YAML mapping |
| `schema.json` | a key the schema does not know, or a wrong type |
| `workflow.initial_state_unknown`, `workflow.initial_state_terminal` | `initial` names no state, or a terminal one |
| `workflow.no_terminal_state`, `workflow.terminal_unreachable` | the work item could never end |
| `workflow.no_human_state` | no state waits for a person |
| `workflow.no_verify_before_pr` | a pull request is opened without a verification step |
| `workflow.implicit_effect` | an effect deduced from a state's name: write `does` or `production` |
| `workflow.name_reserved` | a reserved workflow name |
| `state.unknown`, `state.orphan`, `state.no_inbound` | a state that is not declared, or that nothing leads to |
| `actor.unknown`, `actor.unused` | an actor that is not declared, or never used |
| `actor.group_empty`, `actor.group_placeholder`, `actor.group_unknown` | a human actor's group that is empty, a placeholder or unknown |
| `transition.unbounded_retry` | a step that goes back without `on_fail.max_attempts` |
| `transition.does_requires_system` | `does` on a transition whose actor is not `system` |
| `transition.pull_request_without_open_pr` | `pull_request` on a transition that does not open one |
| `gate.unknown`, `gate.nothing_to_check`, `gate.output_schema`, `gate.already_fixed_not_an_exit` | a gate that does not exist, has nothing to check, or is misused |
| `action.not_system`, `action.on_fail_missing`, `action.effect_unknown`, `action.date_field_unknown`, `action.date_field_not_date` | a governed action declared on the wrong actor, without a way out, or with an unknown effect or date field |
| `decision.output_collision`, `decision.threshold_without_human`, `decision.gateway_unsupported`, `decision.model_usage` | a decision step whose outputs collide, without a person behind a threshold, or a gateway or model that cannot decide |
| `policy.*` | a policy setting the platform does not enforce (a warning) |

Other codes you may meet: `skill.slug_reserved` (a reserved skill name), `agent_incomplete` (an agent
version missing what a step needs).

---

## Glossary

| Word | Means |
| --- | --- |
| **A2A door** | the endpoint that serves workflows as skills of the A2A protocol to applications and other agents ([guide](../integrate/a2a.md)) |
| **Action** | a governed change in an external system (an account created, a pull request merged): proposed, approved when required, done once, compensable |
| **Actor** | who moves a work item: an agent, a person (`human`), the platform (`system`), a `job`, a `decision` model |
| **Agent** | an entry of the agent registry: instructions, a model or code, skills, tools, limits and budget, in versions ([Build an agent](../build/agents.md)) |
| **Application** | an account an application uses to call the A2A door under its own name, on one project; it never decides |
| **Artefact** | a document or file a step produced, stored with its digest |
| **Backend** | the coding agent that runs a step (`claude-code`, `codex`, `gemini-cli`, …) |
| **Budget** | what a run, a work item, a project or an agent may spend, in USD, enforced at the model gateway |
| **Connector** | Choregos's link to an external system: a tracker, a repository, CI, a directory, an MCP server |
| **Decision** | a person's choice at a human step (approve, reject, answer), taken in the console, never by a token |
| **Egress** | the network a run or the platform may reach; opened host by host ([Tools](../build/tools.md#network)) |
| **Gate** | a check a transition requires, read from evidence rather than from what an agent says ([list](workflow-yaml.md#gates)) |
| **Integrations page** | the console page that gives each client (assistants, CLI, REST, A2A) its exact setup |
| **MCP door** | the endpoint that serves Choregos to AI assistants over the Model Context Protocol ([guide](../integrate/mcp.md)) |
| **MCP server** | a server of tools an agent may call, added by the organisation and governed tool by tool |
| **Organisation** | the tenant: its members, projects, agents, skills and connectors, isolated from the others |
| **Plugin** | a versioned package of agents, skills, templates and servers ([guide](../build/plugins.md)) |
| **Policy** | a project's rules: budgets, scope, sandbox, network; it can only tighten the organisation's ceiling |
| **Project** | where work happens: its workflows, connectors, members and policy; written `org:slug` |
| **Release train** | scheduled departures that ship merged work to an environment, with a person's approval |
| **Run** | one execution of an agent or a job for one step of a work item, with its journal and its cost |
| **Skill** | a folder an agent carries: a `SKILL.md` saying when to use it, and its files ([guide](../build/skills.md)) |
| **State** | where a work item stands in its workflow |
| **Token** | a secret that acts as a person or an application, with a scope: `*`, `mcp:read`, `mcp:write`, `a2a` |
| **Transition** | a move from one state to another, by an actor, under gates |
| **Trigger** | a URL another system POSTs JSON to, to open a work item ([guide](../integrate/triggers.md)) |
| **Work item** | one piece of work moving through a workflow: a request, a change, a ticket |
| **Workflow** | the state machine a work item follows, written in YAML ([reference](workflow-yaml.md)) |

---

## Reference

The pages to look things up in, once you know what you want to do.

- [Workflow YAML](workflow-yaml.md): every key of a workflow, its gates, and two complete examples.
- [Error codes](errors.md): what the A2A door, the MCP door, triggers and the REST API answer when
  they refuse.
- [API overview](api.md): the REST API's conventions and resources, and its OpenAPI document.
- [CLI reference](../cli/reference.md): every command, generated from the CLI.
- [Glossary](glossary.md): the words Choregos uses.

---

## Workflow YAML

A workflow is a state machine: **states** a work item can be in, **actors** who move it (agents,
people, the system, jobs, decision models), and **transitions** that say who moves it from where to
where, under which **gates**. This page lists every key. Both examples below are parsed by the
platform's own validator in the repository's tests, and the list of keys is checked against the
workflow schema: a key added to the schema without this page turns the build red.

Check a file before publishing it:

```bash
choregos workflow validate ship-a-change.yaml
choregos workflow show ship-a-change.yaml --process
```

### A complete example

The `ship-a-change` workflow of a development project: an agent refines the request, the product
owner approves the specification, an agent implements it under gates, another verifies, the platform
opens and merges the pull request, and a release train ships it.

```yaml
apiVersion: choregos/v1
kind: Workflow
metadata:
  name: ship-a-change
  version: 1
  description: Refinement, approval, implementation, verification, pull request, merge, release.
  inputs:
    type: object
    required: [ticket]
    properties:
      ticket: { type: string }
      priority: { type: string, enum: [low, high] }
actors:
  refiner: { type: agent, role: refine, model: "profile:standard" }
  owner: { type: human, group: product-owners, sla_hours: 24 }
  dev: { type: agent, role: implement, model: "profile:by_size" }
  checker: { type: agent, role: verify, model: "profile:standard" }
  ci: { type: system }
  captain: { type: human, group: release-captains, sla_hours: 4 }
states:
  inbox: { display: To triage, kind: wait, tracker: { status: Todo, label: "choregos:inbox" } }
  refining: { display: Refining, tracker: { status: Refining } }
  awaiting_spec_approval: { display: Spec to approve, kind: wait, tracker: { status: Needs review } }
  ready: { display: Ready, tracker: { status: Ready } }
  in_progress: { display: In progress, tracker: { status: In progress } }
  verifying: { display: Verifying, tracker: { status: Verifying } }
  pr_open: { display: PR open, kind: wait, tracker: { status: In review } }
  merged: { display: Merged, tracker: { status: Merged } }
  deployed_prod: { display: In production, terminal: true, production: true, tracker: { status: Done } }
  needs_human: { display: Needs a human, kind: wait, tracker: { status: Blocked } }
  abandoned: { display: Abandoned, terminal: true, outcome: cancelled, tracker: { status: Cancelled } }
transitions:
  - id: t-refine
    from: inbox
    to: awaiting_spec_approval
    by: refiner
    outputs: [spec_markdown, size, risk]
    on_fail: { to: inbox, max_attempts: 2, escalate_to: needs_human }
  - id: t-approve-spec
    from: awaiting_spec_approval
    to: ready
    by: owner
    on_reject: refining
    timeout_hours: 72
  - id: t-refine-again
    from: refining
    to: awaiting_spec_approval
    by: refiner
    on_fail: { to: refining, max_attempts: 2, escalate_to: needs_human }
  - id: t-implement
    from: ready
    to: in_progress
    by: dev
    inputs: [spec_markdown, allowed_paths]
    gates: [scope_respected, { name: diff_size_max, params: { files: 60 } }, no_secrets]
    on_fail: { to: ready, max_attempts: 2, escalate_to: needs_human }
  - id: t-verify
    from: in_progress
    to: verifying
    by: checker
    inputs: [spec_markdown]
    gates: [evidence_present]
    on_fail: { to: in_progress, max_attempts: 2, escalate_to: needs_human }
  - id: t-open-pr
    from: verifying
    to: pr_open
    by: ci
    does: open_pr
    pull_request: { draft: false }
    gates: [evidence_present]
    on_fail: { to: verifying, max_attempts: 2, escalate_to: needs_human }
  - id: t-merge
    from: pr_open
    to: merged
    by: ci
    does: merge_pr
    gates: [ci_green, review_approved, scans_ok]
    timeout_hours: 48
    on_fail: { to: in_progress, max_attempts: 3, escalate_to: needs_human }
  - id: t-deploy
    from: merged
    to: deployed_prod
    via: release_train
    train: { env: prod, approval: captain }
    timeout_hours: 72
  - id: t-abandon
    from: needs_human
    to: abandoned
    by: owner
    timeout_hours: 168
artifacts:
  diff: { show: facts, title: Changes }
budget:
  ticket_usd: 6
  on_exceeded: needs_human
a2a:
  skill: ship-a-change
  description: Ship a change through review and release.
  input_modes: [text/plain, application/json]
defaults:
  from_any_agent_state:
    on_question: needs_human
    on_budget_exceeded: needs_human
    on_timeout: needs_human
  needs_human:
    on_answer: resume
    on_abandon: abandoned
```

### Top level

| Key | Required | What it is |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `apiVersion` | yes | always `choregos/v1` |
| `kind` | yes | always `Workflow` |
| `metadata` | yes | the workflow's name, version and inputs ([below](#metadata)) |
| `actors` | yes | who moves work items, by name ([below](#actors)) |
| `states` | yes | where a work item can be, by name ([below](#states)) |
| `transitions` | yes | who moves it from where to where ([below](#transitions)) |
| `defaults` | no | what happens on a question, a spent budget, a timeout ([below](#defaults)) |
| `budget` | no | what a work item may spend ([below](#budget)) |
| `artifacts` | no | how each output is typed and shown ([below](#artifacts)) |
| `a2a` | no | serve the workflow as an A2A skill ([below](#a2a)) |
| `initial` | no | the state a work item starts in; the first declared state when absent |

Names of states, actors and transition ids are lower-case letters, digits, `-` and `_`, 63 characters
at most.

### `metadata`

| Key | What it is |
| --- | --- |
| `name` | the workflow's name in the project: lower-case letters, digits and `-` |
| `version` | an integer from 1 |
| `description` | one sentence |
| `extends` | `template:<name>@<version>`: start from a shipped template |
| `inputs` | the JSON Schema of a work item's fields; every door (console, CLI, REST, MCP, A2A, triggers) checks fields against it |
| `catalogue` | how the workflow catalogue presents it: `title` (80 characters), `summary` (400), `tags` (12 at most); the engine ignores it |

### `actors`

Each actor has a `type`.

| `type` | Keys | What it is |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `agent` | `role` (required), `agent`, `model`, `backend`, `playbook`, `max_turns`, `max_minutes`, `fresh_context` | an agent run in a sandbox. `agent` names a registry agent (`slug` or `slug@version`) whose version sets the instructions, model, limits and budget ([Build an agent](../build/agents.md)). `model` is `profile:<name>`, `profile:by_size` (the default, by the work item's size) or a model id. `backend` is the coding agent, the project's default otherwise. `playbook` names the instructions when there is no registry agent (the role's own otherwise). `fresh_context: true` starts without the previous runs' context |
| `human` | `group` (required), `sla_hours`, `escalate_to` | a person of the identity provider's group decides in the console |
| `system` | none | the platform itself: opens or merges a pull request (`does`), proposes an action |
| `job` | `role` and `command` (required), `image`, `max_minutes` | a command run in the step's sandbox, without a model: `command` is an argument list, never a shell line; `image` is a job image the operator named. The facts it writes in `.choregos/facts.json` are measured |
| `decision` | `role`, `questions`, `state` (required), `model`, `timeout_seconds` | a decision model answers typed questions about the work item, without a sandbox. `state` lists what it reads (`title`, `description`, `labels`, `type`, `fields.<name>`, `outputs.<name>`). Each question writes an output `<name>` and `<name>_confidence`, which `when` reads |

A decision question has a `type`, `instructions` (what is asked, 2,000 characters) and, by type:
`yes_no` (nothing more), `choice` with `options` (2 to 100), `score` with ordered `levels` (2 to 10,
lowest first).

The roles of the shipped playbooks (`triage`, `refine`, `plan`, `implement`, `verify`, `review`,
`fix_ci`, `address_review`, `release_notes`, `verify_prod`, `custom`) keep their meaning; any other
name is yours.

### `states`

| Key | Default | What it is |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `display` | required | the name people read |
| `kind` | `work` | `work` (an actor is acting), `wait` (waiting for a person or an event) or `terminal` |
| `terminal` | `false` | the work item ends here |
| `outcome` | `success` | how a terminal state ends it: `success`, `declined` or `cancelled` |
| `production` | `false` | a production state, reachable only `via: release_train` |
| `tracker` | | how an external tracker shows it: `status` and `label` |

### `transitions`

A transition has `from` and `to`, and either `by` (an actor) or `via: release_train` with `train`.

| Key | What it is |
| --- | --- |
| `id` | a stable name for the transition; the console and the journal use it |
| `from` | a state, or `*agent` for any state an agent drives |
| `to` | the state it leads to |
| `by` | the actor that performs it |
| `via` | `release_train`: the work item ships with the next departure of a release train |
| `train` | with `via`: `env` (required), `approval` (a human actor who approves the departure), `auto_sync` |
| `gates` | the checks that must pass before the work item moves ([gates](#gates)): a name, or `name` and `params` |
| `inputs` | the documents and files the step receives |
| `outputs` | the documents the step must produce |
| `output_types` | the type of each output: `markdown`, `json`, `mermaid`, `sarif`, `text`, `csv`, `html`, `pdf`, `docx`, `xlsx`, `pptx`, `png`, `jpeg`, `gif`, `webp`, `svg`, `mp4`, `webm`, `file`, `diff`, `level`, `metric`, `keyvalue` |
| `when` | take this transition only when the last step's outputs match ([below](#when)) |
| `on_fail` | what happens when the step or a gate fails: `to`, `max_attempts`, `escalate_to` (all three required) |
| `on_reject` | for a human step: the state a rejection sends the work item to |
| `on_changes_requested` | for a review: like `on_fail`, when changes are requested |
| `review` | who reviews: `agents` (actor names), `humans` (`group`, and `required`: `always`, `by_policy` or `never`) |
| `timeout_hours` | how long the step may wait |
| `does` | what the platform does on a system transition: `open_pr` or `merge_pr` |
| `pull_request` | with `does: open_pr`: `draft: true` opens it as a draft |
| `task` | a form a person fills: `form` (a JSON Schema whose properties become fields), `title`, `instructions`, `attest` (what the person attests, word for word) |
| `action` | a governed action the system proposes ([below](#action)) |
| `spawn` | a fan-out: one child work item per element of a list ([below](#spawn)) |

#### `when`

Every key is an output name of the last step; every condition must hold. Among the transitions
leaving a state, the first whose `when` holds is taken, and one without `when` is the default. A
condition is a value (equal), a list (one of), or an object of `equals`, `in`, `not_in`, `gt`, `gte`,
`lt`, `lte`. A missing output never matches.

#### `action`

`kind`, `title` and `effects` are required. Each effect has an `effect` (an operation of a
connector), `with` (its arguments) and `compensate` (how to undo it). `justification` and `params` are
rendered with the work item's fields; `not_before` delays it to a date taken from a field
(`fields.start_date - 10d`). `approval` asks people first: `approvers` (each a `role`, a `group`, and
`min` people), `step_up_minutes` (they must have signed in within that time), `separation_of_duties`
(the requester cannot approve).

#### `spawn`

`workflow` (the children's, in the same project), `for_each` (the list walked, such as
`fields.symbols` or `outputs.candidates`) and `title` are required; `fields` renders each child's
fields; `max_children` (20 by default), `succeeded` (the children's states that count as a success)
and `min_succeeded` decide when the transition passes.

### `defaults`

| Key | What it is |
| --- | --- |
| `from_any_agent_state.on_question` | where a work item goes when an agent asks a question |
| `from_any_agent_state.on_budget_exceeded` | where it goes when its budget is spent |
| `from_any_agent_state.on_timeout` | where it goes when a step runs out of time |
| `needs_human.on_answer` | `resume`: once a person answers, the work item goes back where it was |
| `needs_human.on_abandon` | where it goes when the person abandons it |

### `budget`

`ticket_usd` is what one work item may spend, which can only tighten the project's policy;
`on_exceeded` is the state a work item goes to when it is spent.

### `artifacts`

How each output is shown, by output name: `type` (`level`, `metric` or `keyvalue`), `title`, `show`
(`facts` on the work item's *About* card, `tab` by default, `hidden`), and for a scale either `scale`
(`risk`, `size`, `verdict`) or `levels` (each a `value`, a `title` and a `tone`: `neutral`, `info`,
`ok`, `warn`, `danger`), with `unit`, `min`, `max` and `better` (`higher` or `lower`) for a metric.

### `a2a`

Serves the workflow as a skill of the A2A door: `skill` and `description` (required), `input_modes`
(`[text/plain]` by default). See [Start a workflow over A2A](../integrate/a2a.md).

### Gates

A gate checks; it does not trust what the agent says. The synchronous ones rule at once from the step's
result and the diff; the others wait for an event.

| Gate | Checks |
| --- | --- |
| `scope_respected` | the change stays inside the allowed paths and out of the denied ones |
| `diff_size_max` | the change touches at most `params.files` files |
| `no_secrets` | the change adds no secret |
| `evidence_present` | the step brought its evidence (tests that ran, coverage) |
| `evidence_facts` | the facts a trade named are there, and comparable if asked |
| `outputs_present` | the declared outputs exist and are not empty |
| `outputs_in` | named outputs take an allowed value: `params.values` |
| `output_schema` | named outputs match a JSON Schema: `params.schemas` |
| `numbers_measured` | every number an agent writes comes from a measured document |
| `tool_called` | the tools the step required were really called, read from the ledger |
| `coverage_delta_min` | test coverage does not drop below the threshold |
| `docs_updated` | the branch updates the documentation when it changes anything else |
| `markdown_sections` | the documents the branch adds carry their required sections |
| `adr_number_free` | the number of an ADR the branch adds is not already taken |
| `already_fixed_proven` | the fix is already on the default branch, on measured evidence |
| `ci_green` | the pull request's CI passed (waits) |
| `review_approved` | the pull request was approved (waits) |
| `scans_ok` | the security scans passed (waits) |
| `provenance_signed` | the build's provenance is signed (waits) |
| `flag_present` | a high-risk work item names a feature flag that exists (waits) |
| `action_succeeded` | the transition's governed action succeeded (waits) |
| `external` | an external system reported its verdict (waits) |

### A second example: decisions, a job, conditions

A decision model sorts incoming bugs, a job reproduces the reproducible ones, the rest goes to a lead:

```yaml
apiVersion: choregos/v1
kind: Workflow
metadata:
  name: bug-triage
  version: 1
  description: A decision model sorts incoming bugs; a job reproduces them; a person takes the rest.
  inputs:
    type: object
    properties:
      ticket: { type: string }
  catalogue:
    title: Bug triage
    summary: Sort incoming bugs and reproduce the ones that can be.
    tags: [software, triage]
actors:
  sorter:
    type: decision
    role: triage
    state: [title, description, labels]
    questions:
      kind: { type: choice, instructions: "Is this a bug, a feature request or a question?", options: [bug, feature, question] }
      reproducible: { type: yes_no, instructions: "Does the report give steps to reproduce?" }
  reproducer: { type: job, role: reproduce, command: ["make", "reproduce"], max_minutes: 15 }
  lead: { type: human, group: developers, sla_hours: 8 }
states:
  inbox: { display: New, kind: wait }
  sorted: { display: Sorted }
  reproduced: { display: Reproduced, kind: wait }
  with_lead: { display: With the lead, kind: wait }
  closed: { display: Closed, terminal: true }
  declined: { display: Not a bug, terminal: true, outcome: declined }
transitions:
  - id: t-sort
    from: inbox
    to: sorted
    by: sorter
  - id: t-reproduce
    from: sorted
    to: reproduced
    by: reproducer
    when: { kind: bug, reproducible: true, reproducible_confidence: { gte: 0.8 } }
    outputs: [reproduction]
    gates: [outputs_present]
    on_fail: { to: sorted, max_attempts: 1, escalate_to: with_lead }
  - id: t-not-a-bug
    from: sorted
    to: declined
    by: sorter
    when: { kind: { in: [feature, question] } }
  - id: t-to-lead
    from: sorted
    to: with_lead
    by: sorter
  - id: t-close
    from: reproduced
    to: closed
    by: lead
  - id: t-close-by-hand
    from: with_lead
    to: closed
    by: lead
artifacts:
  reproduction: { show: tab, title: Reproduction }
budget:
  ticket_usd: 2
  on_exceeded: with_lead
```

### When the validator refuses

Each problem has a code, a line and a column. The most frequent:

| Code | Means |
| --- | --- |
| `schema.json` | a key the schema does not know, or a value of the wrong type |
| `yaml.syntax` | the file is not YAML |
| `state.unknown`, `actor.unknown`, `gate.unknown` | a name that is not declared (or not a known gate) |
| `state.orphan`, `state.no_inbound` | a state nothing leads to |
| `workflow.no_terminal_state`, `workflow.terminal_unreachable` | the work item could never end |
| `transition.unbounded_retry` | an agent or job step that goes back to an earlier state without `on_fail.max_attempts` |
| `transition.does_requires_system` | `does` on a transition whose actor is not `system` |
| `workflow.no_verify_before_pr` | a pull request opened without a verification step (a warning) |

The complete list is in [Error codes](errors.md#workflow-validation).
